newsitem.title: USA: Circle pleased with Miami airport.
newsitem.headline: Circle pleased with Miami airport.

text.p: Circle International, the big freight forwarder, struggles with bottlenecks at Miami International Airport, but executives told Reuters on Thursday the problems are no worse than at many other airports.
"There are logjams during peak periods," said George Kulovic, regional manager in Miami for the company, a unit of San Francisco-based Harper Group Inc.

"But there is no alternative to Miami for Latin American cargo," Kulovic said, noting that other gateways struggle with the same lack of flight frequency and other problems. And he said Miami has a huge and sophisticated transportation infrastructure that other potential Latin American gateways lack.
"It is no worse than other airports," said Kulovic, "We think London has backlogs," he said.
Miami is Circle's largest operation worldwide with warehouse space of 225,000 square feet. Circle has 42 offices in Latin America, mostly company-owned.
Circle's Miami operation handles logistics and forwarding of mostly dry goods for companies doing business in Latin America.
"We have handled a lot of computers, but it will be an increasing amount of telecommunications equipment. There will be a lot of infrastructure (business) in Latin America," Kulovic said.
Circle's Latam business has been strong for years, and Kulovic expects that strength to continue.
The sharp rise in jet fuel and the resulting increased shipping costs is having "a tremendous impact," on shippers, said Dominick Bargione, the company's Miami air export manager.
As the higher fuel costs are passed from the airlines to the forwarders and then to the shipper "the burden will end up on the people paying for the goods," Bargione said.
Circle calls itself the largest air freight and logistics provider to Latin America. -- Air Cargo Newsroom Tel+44 171 542 7706 Fax+44 171 542 5017
